proposal.motivation: LiAlSiO4 (mp-aaaaajjj) and Li3AlSiO5 (mp-aaacgaxr) gave the best contact penalty so far (0.204 eV, bin 10), better than Li3PO4 (bin 16), LiF (bin 26), Li3BO3 (bin 15) and Li5Al(SiO4)2 (bin 36), so the Al/Si oxide family is the most promising lead.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2Si2O5 is a silicate built only from non-reducible Si4+ with a high Si:Li ratio. The best result so far, LiAl(SiO3)2 (bin 7), had the lowest Li content among the Al/Si oxides, and the Li-richer orthosilicates (Li5Al(SiO4)2, bin 36) did worse. Extending that trend to a Si-rich, Li-poor chain silicate may lower the sulfide reduction penalty further.
proposal.motivation: LiAl(SiO3)2 (mp-aaabfuqq) gave the best penalty so far (0.147 eV, bin 7). Li-richer members (Li5Al(SiO4)2, Li3AlSiO5, LiAlSiO4) were worse or equal, which suggests lower Li content and higher Si content reduce the sulfide reaction.

proposal.hypothesis: LiAlB2O5 combines non-reducible Al3+ and B3+ with a Li-poor, borate-rich framework. The best contact penalty so far came from LiAl(SiO3)2 (bin 7), which is Al-rich and Li-poor among the Al/Si oxides. Replacing Si with B may keep the Al-O bonding that resists sulfide reduction while changing the reaction energy with Li6PS5Cl.
proposal.motivation: LiAl(SiO3)2 (mp-aaabfuqq) gave the best penalty so far (0.147 eV, bin 7). Li-richer Al/Si oxides were worse (bins 10 and 36), which suggests lower Li content helps. Li3BO3 gave bin 15, so a borate with Al is a reasonable test of the Al-oxide chemistry.
